key_insight: A data-driven impeller wall model lets LES of von Kármán flow reproduce long-time mean behavior and reveal slow metastable state switching that blade-resolved simulations cannot reach affordably.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical reduced-cost path for simulating high-Re turbulent impeller-driven systems when direct resolution of rotating hardware is too expensive.
method: Parametrize impeller-region velocity with B-splines and apply it as momentum forcing in LES.
Initialize coefficients with ODIL constrained by RANS, PIV data, and torque measurements.
Refine the model with CMA-ES to match LES time-averaged velocity and torque to experiments.
evidence_signal: The model is evaluated against experimental PIV and torque data and then used in long-duration LES, which reproduces the bulk mean flow and metastable switching dynamics.
watch_item: Because the impeller action is inferred from limited experimental observables and optimized for averages, the model may be sensitive to measurement coverage and may not fully capture all instantaneous near-impeller physics.
paper_title: Optimal, Data-Driven Wall Models for Efficient Large Eddy Simulations of Metastable von Kármán Flows
